description: CLAIM: GitHub Trending has NO official API. Evidence op 1: GitHub's own REST API root directory (api.github.com — the machine-readable index of every endpoint template) contains no 'trending' entry (expect gate fails the run the day GitHub ships one). Evidence op 2+3: the HTML page at github.com/trending is therefore the only first-party source — fetched raw and parsed engine-inline (deno-dom) at Source Ladder L4, a downgrade forced by the proven absence of L1 (that absence IS this claim). Tab-free: no browser, no login, no extension — runs anywhere including CI. Returns {outcome, reason, api_directory_has_trending, repo_count, repos}.
return: {'outcome': dyn(size(observe.repos) > 0 ? 'ok' : 'empty'), 'reason': dyn(size(observe.repos) > 0 ? '' : 'trending page markup drifted — article.Box-row h2 a matched nothing'), 'api_directory_has_trending': dyn(observe.api_root.contains('trending')), 'repo_count': dyn(double(size(observe.repos))), 'repos': dyn(observe.repos)}
source_intent: Prove nightly that GitHub Trending has no official API (api.github.com directory contains no trending endpoint) and that the HTML page remains the only first-party source, by deterministically extracting the current trending repos from it at zero tokens.
